verbalization: Tenoxicam and Cyp2c9 are linked through a cascade of molecular interactions that involve nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). The evidence suggests that Tenoxicam causes gastrointestinal ulcers, which are then caused by Oxaprozin, a NSAID. Oxaprozin binds to Cyp2c9, indicating a direct interaction between the drug and the enzyme. This pathway highlights a recurring mechanism where NSAIDs, through their effects on the gastrointestinal tract, trigger a chain of events that ultimately involve the cytochrome P450 2C9 enzyme. The lowest common ancestor of Tenoxicam and Oxaprozin, both NSAIDs, further supports the notion of a shared pharmacological pathway. The integration of these interactions underscores the role of Cyp2c9 in mediating the effects of NSAIDs, particularly in the context of gastrointestinal inflammation.
